title.zh: 卷四百一十 列傳第一百六十九 婁機 沈煥 舒璘 曹彥約 范應鈴 徐經孫
title.en: Volume 410 Biographies 169: Lou Ji, Shen Huan, Shu Lin, Cao Yanyue, Fan Yingling, Xu Jingsun
title.raw: 卷四百一十 列傳第一百六十九 婁機 沈煥 舒璘 曹彥約 范應鈴 徐經孫 Volume 410 Biographies 169: Lou Ji, Shen Huan, Shu Lin, Cao Yanyue, Fan Yingling, Xu Jingsun

sentences.zh: 婁機沈煥

translations.literal: Lou Ji, Shen Huan
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ji and Shen Huan

sentences.zh: 〈（舒璘附）〉

translations.literal: (with appended biography of Shu Lin)
translations.idiomatic: (with appended biography of Shu Lin)

sentences.zh: 曹彥約範應鈴徐經孫

translations.literal: Cao Yanyue, Fan Yingling, Xu Jingsun
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue, Fan Yingling, and Xu Jingsun

sentences.zh: 婁機，字彥發，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Lou Ji, style name Yanfa, was a man of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ji, whose style name was Yanfa, came from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年進士，授鹽官尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao he became a jinshi and was appointed salt commissioner of Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Qiandao (1166) and was appointed salt commissioner of Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，調含山主簿。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was transferred to be registrar of Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he left office for mourning; when the mourning period ended he was assigned as registrar of Hanshan.

sentences.zh: 郡委治銅城圩八十有四，役夫三千有奇，設廬以處之，器用材植，一出於官，民樂勸趨，兩旬告畢。

translations.literal: The prefecture entrusted him with managing eighty-four polders at Tongcheng, with more than three thousand laborers; he set up lodges to house them, and all tools, materials, and timber came from the government; the people gladly hastened to the work, and it was reported complete within twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture put him in charge of eighty-four polders at Tongcheng with a labor force of more than three thousand. He built lodges to house the workers and supplied all tools, materials, and timber from official stores. The people worked willingly, and the project was finished within twenty days.

sentences.zh: 七攝鄰邑，率以治績聞。

translations.literal: Seven times he took charge of neighboring counties, and in each case his administrative achievements became known.
translations.idiomatic: On seven occasions he was sent to administer neighboring counties, and each time his record of good governance won notice.

sentences.zh: 調於潛縣丞，輕賦稅，正版籍，簡獄訟，興學校。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be assistant magistrate of Yuqian, where he lightened taxes, corrected household registers, simplified litigation, and established schools.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to serve as assistant magistrate of Yuqian, he reduced tax burdens, straightened out household registers, streamlined court cases, and revived the schools.

sentences.zh: 遭外艱，免喪，為江東提舉司幹辦公事，易淮東，已而復舊，改知西安縣。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for a parent-in-law; when the mourning ended he served as staff officer of the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was moved to Huaidong, then returned to his former post, and was changed to magistrate of Xi'an County.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife's parent died he left office for mourning. After mourning he served as a staff officer on the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was briefly transferred to Huaidong, then returned to Jiangdong and was appointed magistrate of Xi'an County.

sentences.zh: 巨室買地為塋域，發地遇石，復索元價。

translations.literal: A great household bought land for a burial ground; when the ground was opened and stone was encountered, they again demanded the original price.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful family bought land for a cemetery. When excavation turned up rock, they demanded a refund of the purchase price.

sentences.zh: 機曰：“設得金，將誰歸？

translations.literal: Ji said: "Suppose gold were found—who would it belong to?
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ji said, "If gold were found there, who would it belong to?

sentences.zh: ”通判饒州，平反冤獄。

translations.literal: " He served as vice-prefect of Raozhou and redressed wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: " As vice-prefect of Raozhou he overturned wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 蜀帥袁說友辟參議幕中，不就，改幹辦諸司審計司。

translations.literal: The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuiyou invited him into his staff as counselor, but he did not accept and was changed to staff officer of the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuiyou invited him to join his staff as a counselor, but he declined and was instead appointed a staff officer in the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.

sentences.zh: 轉對，請裁損經費，又論刑名疑慮之敝。

translations.literal: At the rotating audience he requested cuts in expenditures and also discussed the abuses arising from doubtful points in criminal law.
translations.idiomatic: At an audience with the emperor he urged reductions in government spending and criticized abuses caused by ambiguous provisions in criminal law.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正寺主簿，為太常博士、秘書郎，請續編《中興館閣書目》，又請寬恤淮、浙被旱州縣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to registrar of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and secretary of the Secretariat, requested continuation of the compilation of the "Catalogue of the Zhongxing Hall of Literature," and also requested relief for Huai and Zhe counties stricken by drought.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to registrar of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan, he served as an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and as a secretary in the Secretariat. He petitioned to continue compiling the "Catalogue of the Zhongxing Hall of Literature" and asked for relief for drought-stricken counties in the Huai and Zhe regions.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子始就外傅，遴選學官，以機兼資善堂小學教授。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent had just begun to study under an outside tutor; academic officials were selected, and Ji was made concurrently elementary instructor at the Hall for Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince first began studying under outside tutors, academic officials were chosen, and Lou Ji was appointed concurrently as elementary instructor at the Hall for Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 機日陳正言正道，又以累朝事親、修身、治國、愛民四事，手書以獻，太子置之坐右，朝夕觀省。

translations.literal: Ji daily presented upright words and the correct Way, and also copied by hand for presentation the four topics of honoring parents, cultivating the self, governing the state, and loving the people as treated by successive dynasties; the heir apparent placed them at his right hand and viewed them morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Each day Lou Ji lectured on upright conduct and the proper Way. He also copied by hand and presented teachings on honoring parents, self-cultivation, governing the state, and caring for the people as drawn from successive dynasties. The crown prince kept these writings at his right hand and read them morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 隨事開明，多所裨益。

translations.literal: As matters arose he clarified them, and was of much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He clarified matters as they arose and proved of great benefit to the prince.

sentences.zh: 遷太常丞，仍兼資善。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while still holding the concurrent post at the Hall for Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he continued to serve concurrently at the Hall for Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 旋遷右曹郎官、秘書省著作郎，改兼駕部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was moved to be a bureau secretary of the right section and compiler in the Secretariat, and was changed to hold concurrently the post in the Department of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to serve as a bureau secretary of the right section and as a compiler in the Secretariat, and was reassigned to hold a concurrent post in the Department of Transport.

sentences.zh: 都城大火，機應詔上封事，力言朝臣務為奉承，不能出己見以裨國論；

translations.literal: When a great fire broke out in the capital, Ji responded to an imperial edict with a sealed memorial, forcefully stating that court officials strove only to flatter and could not offer their own views to benefit national deliberations;
translations.idiomatic: After a great fire swept the capital, Lou Ji submitted a sealed memorial by imperial command. He argued forcefully that court officials cared only about flattery and would not offer independent views to strengthen state policy;

sentences.zh: 外臣不稱職，至苛刻以困民財；

translations.literal: local officials were unfit for their posts, going so far as to be harsh and thereby straining the people's wealth;
translations.idiomatic: local officials were incompetent, some so harsh that they drained the people's resources;

sentences.zh: 將帥偏裨務為交結，而不知訓閱以強軍律。

translations.literal: generals and subordinate commanders strove to form connections and did not know how to drill and review troops to strengthen military discipline.
translations.idiomatic: and generals and their subordinates busied themselves with networking rather than drilling troops to enforce military discipline.

sentences.zh: 時年七十，丐閑，不許。

translations.literal: At that time he was seventy years old and requested leisure, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was then seventy years old and asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 太子得機所著《廣幹祿字》一編，尤喜，命戴溪跋之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent obtained a copy of Ji's work "Expanded Characters for the Thousand-Character Classic" and was especially pleased, ordering Dai Xi to write a colophon for it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince obtained a copy of Lou Ji's "Expanded Characters for the Thousand-Character Classic" and was especially pleased with it. He ordered Dai Xi to write a colophon.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史，講未退而除命頒，太子戀戀幾不忍舍，機亦為之感涕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to investigating censor; before his lecture had ended the appointment order was issued; the heir apparent was deeply attached and could hardly bear to let him go, and Ji too was moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor. The appointment arrived before his lecture had ended. The crown prince was so attached to him that he could hardly bear to let him go, and Lou Ji wept as well.

sentences.zh: 論京官必兩任、有舉主、年三十以上，方許作縣。

translations.literal: He argued that capital officials must have served two terms, have a recommender, and be over thirty years of age before being allowed to serve as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that capital officials should be required to have served two terms, have a sponsor, and be at least thirty before they could be appointed county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 又論郡守輕濫太甚，貽害千里。

translations.literal: He also argued that prefects were appointed too lightly and casually, doing harm for a thousand li around.
translations.idiomatic: He also warned that prefects were being appointed far too casually, to the harm of entire circuits.

sentences.zh: 蘇師旦怙勢妄作，蒙蔽自肆，語及者皆罪去，而獨憚機。

translations.literal: Su Shidan relied on power and acted recklessly, deceiving others and indulging himself at will; whoever spoke of him was punished and removed, yet he alone feared Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shidan abused his power, acted recklessly, deceived others, and did as he pleased. Anyone who spoke against him was punished and dismissed, yet he alone feared Lou Ji.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄議開邊，機極口沮之，謂：“恢復之名非不美，今士卒驕逸，遽驅於鋒鏑之下，人才難得，財力未裕，萬一兵連禍結，久而不解，奈何？

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou discussed opening the frontier; Ji strongly dissuaded him in speech, saying: "The name 'recovery' is not unbeautiful, but now the soldiers are arrogant and lax; to drive them hastily under spear and blade, talent is hard to obtain and finances are not ample—if by chance warfare links up with disaster and drags on unresolved, what then?
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou proposed reopening military campaigns on the frontier, Lou Ji strongly opposed him, saying, "The goal of recovering lost territory is admirable in name, but the troops are now arrogant and undisciplined. To rush them into battle when capable commanders are scarce and finances are strained—if war drags on without end, what then?

sentences.zh: ”侂胄聞之不說，其議愈密，外廷罔測。

translations.literal: " Tuozhou heard this and was displeased; the deliberations grew ever more secret, and the outer court could not fathom them.
translations.idiomatic: " Tuozhou was displeased. War planning grew ever more secret, and the outer court could not guess what was being decided.

sentences.zh: 又上疏極論：“雖密謀人莫得知，而羽書一馳，中外皇惑。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial arguing forcefully: "Although secret plans may be unknown to others, once urgent dispatches are sent flying, court and country alike are thrown into alarm and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial arguing forcefully, "Even if secret plans are unknown to the public, once urgent dispatches fly out, the court and the realm are thrown into alarm and confusion.

sentences.zh: ”侍御史鄧友龍初不知兵，騰書投合，妄薦大將，既召還，專主此議。

translations.literal: " Attending censor Deng Youlong at first knew nothing of military affairs; he sent up writings to curry favor, rashly recommended a great general, and once recalled became the sole advocate of this policy.
translations.idiomatic: " The attending censor Deng Youlong knew nothing of military affairs at first. He sent up writings to curry favor, rashly recommended a commander, and once recalled to court became the chief advocate of war.

sentences.zh: 機語友龍曰：“今日孰可為大將？

translations.literal: Ji said to Youlong: "Today who can serve as great general?
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ji asked Youlong, "Who today is fit to serve as commander-in-chief?

sentences.zh: 孰可為計臣？

translations.literal: Who can serve as planning minister?
translations.idiomatic: Who is fit to serve as chief strategist?

sentences.zh: 正使以殿岩當之，能保其可用乎？”

translations.literal: Even if Dian Yan were put in that role, can you guarantee he would be usable?
translations.idiomatic: Even if you appoint someone as Palace Front commander, can you guarantee he would be effective?

sentences.zh: 遷右正言兼侍講，首論廣蓄人才，乞詔侍從、台諫、學士、待制、三牙管軍各舉將帥邊郡一二人，召問甄拔，優養以備緩急。

translations.literal: He was moved to right rectifier and concurrent lecturer, and first argued for broadly storing talent, requesting an edict that attendants, remonstrators, academicians, designated draftsmen, and the three military bureaus each recommend one or two generals or border officials, summon them for questioning and selection, and nurture them well against emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to right rectifier and concurrent lecturer, he first urged the court to stockpile talent broadly. He asked that attendants, remonstrators, academicians, designated draftsmen, and the three military bureaus each recommend one or two generals or frontier officials, that they be summoned for examination and selection, and that they be supported against future emergencies.

sentences.zh: 進太常少卿兼權中書舍人，詔遣宣諭荊、襄，機昌言曰：“使往慰安人情則可，必欲開邊啟釁，有死而已，不能從也。

translations.literal: He advanced to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting drafting secretary of the Secretariat; an edict sent him to announce and comfort Jing and Xiang; Ji spoke forthrightly, saying: "If the envoy goes to soothe popular sentiment, that is acceptable; but if you must open the frontier and provoke conflict, there is only death—I cannot follow.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting drafting secretary of the Secretariat. When ordered to go announce and reassure the people of Jing and Xiang, Lou Ji spoke bluntly: "If the mission is to comfort the people, I can go. But if the aim is to reopen the frontier and provoke war, I would rather die than obey.

sentences.zh: ”泗州捷聞，愈增憂危，且曰：“若自此成功，以攄列聖之宿憤，老臣雖死亦幸，謫官，但恐進銳退速，禍愈深耳。

translations.literal: " When news of victory at Sizhou arrived, his worry and peril increased yet more, and he said: "If from this point success is achieved and the long-standing grievances of successive emperors are vented, this old official though dead would still be fortunate, demoted official though I am—but I fear advancing sharply and retreating swiftly, with disaster growing deeper.
translations.idiomatic: " When news of victory at Sizhou arrived, his anxiety only grew. He said, "If the campaign succeeds and the grievances of former emperors are finally redressed, I would die content even as a demoted official. But I fear a rash advance followed by a hasty retreat, which would only deepen the disaster.

sentences.zh: ”友龍至不能堪曰：“不逐此人，則異議無所回。

translations.literal: " Youlong could bear it no longer and said: "If this man is not driven out, dissenting views cannot be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: " Deng Youlong could bear it no longer and said, "Unless this man is removed, dissenting voices cannot be silenced.

sentences.zh: ”機遂以言去。

translations.literal: " Ji thereupon left office because of his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Lou Ji was dismissed because of his remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，召為吏部侍郎兼太子左庶子，還朝，言：“至公始可以服天下，權臣以私意橫生，敗國殄民，今當行以至公。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, Ji was summoned as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and left tutor of the heir apparent; returning to court he said: "Only utmost fairness can make the realm submit; powerful ministers have arisen from private intent, ruining the state and destroying the people—now utmost fairness must be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Tuozhou was executed, Lou Ji was recalled as vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and left tutor of the crown prince. On returning to court he said, "Only absolute fairness can win the loyalty of the realm. Powerful ministers have risen through private ambition, ruining the state and harming the people. The court must now govern with absolute fairness.

sentences.zh: 若曰私恩未報，首為汲引，私仇未復，且為沮抑，一涉於私，人心將無所觀感矣。

translations.literal: If one says private favors are not yet repaid and therefore first promotes one's own, or private enmities are not yet avenged and therefore obstructs others, once private feeling is involved the hearts of the people will have nothing by which to be moved and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: If one says private favors remain unrewarded and therefore promotes one's own followers first, or private grudges remain unsettled and therefore blocks one's enemies, once private feeling enters government the people will have nothing to respect or follow.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“兩淮招集敢勇，不難於招而難於處。

translations.literal: " He also said: "In the two Huai regions recruiting the bold and brave is not difficult—what is difficult is managing them.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Recruiting bold fighters in the two Huai regions is not difficult; managing them is.

sentences.zh: 若非繩以紀律，課其勤惰，必為後害。

translations.literal: If they are not bound by discipline and their diligence and laziness assessed, they will surely become a later harm.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they are bound by discipline and judged on diligence and slackness, they will surely become a future menace.

sentences.zh: ”仍請檢校權臣、內侍等沒入家貲，專為養兵之助。

translations.literal: " He still requested verification of confiscated household property of powerful ministers and inner attendants, devoted exclusively to supporting the army.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked that confiscated property of powerful ministers and palace eunuchs be audited and devoted exclusively to supporting the troops.

sentences.zh: 機裏人有故官吏部，喪未舉而子赴調者，機謂彼既冒法禁，而部胥不之問，即撻數吏，使之治葬而後來。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman of Ji who had formerly served in the Ministry of Personnel had not yet conducted the funeral when his son went to report for assignment; Ji said that since he had already violated the law and the ministry clerks did not question it, he immediately flogged several clerks and made the son arrange the funeral before coming.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman who had formerly served in the Ministry of Personnel had not yet held his parent's funeral when his son reported for assignment. Lou Ji said the son had already violated the law and the ministry clerks had failed to stop him. He had several clerks flogged and ordered the son to complete the funeral before reporting for duty.

sentences.zh: 聞者韙之。

translations.literal: Those who heard approved.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard of it approved.

sentences.zh: 兼太子詹事，著《曆代帝王總要》以裨考訂。

translations.literal: He held concurrently the post of tutor of the heir apparent, and compiled the "Essentials of Successive Emperors" to aid verification and collation.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as tutor of the crown prince and compiled the "Essentials of Successive Emperors" to aid historical verification.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 海巡八廂親從、都軍頭、指揮使年勞轉資，恩旨太濫，乞收寢未應年格之人，年已及者予之，帝稱善良久。

translations.literal: For coastal patrol in the eight sections, personal followers, commanders-in-chief, and regimental commanders, promotion by years of service was too lavish in imperial grace; he requested to withhold those not yet meeting the age standard and grant it to those whose years had arrived; the emperor praised his goodness for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions by seniority for coastal patrol officers, personal followers, commanders-in-chief, and regimental commanders had become too lavish. He asked that those not yet meeting the seniority requirement be denied promotion while those who had earned it receive it promptly. The emperor praised his sound judgment at length.

sentences.zh: 飛蝗為災。

translations.literal: Locusts flew and became a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 機應詔言：“和議甫成，先務安靜，葺罅漏以成紀綱，節財用以固邦本，練士卒以壯國威。”

translations.literal: Ji responded to an edict, saying: "The peace agreement has just been concluded; the first task is tranquility—mend cracks and leaks to complete regulations and standards, economize finances to solidify the foundation of the state, drill soldiers and officers to strengthen national prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ji responded to an imperial edict, saying, "The peace treaty has only just been concluded. The first priority must be stability: mend weaknesses to restore order, economize spending to strengthen the state's foundation, and drill the troops to bolster national prestige.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書兼給事中，擢同知樞密院事兼太子賓客，進參知政事。

translations.literal: He was moved to minister of rites while holding concurrently supervising secretary, was elevated to associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and guest of the heir apparent, and advanced to participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of rites while retaining his post as supervising secretary, then elevated to associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and guest of the crown prince, and finally advanced to vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 當幹戈甫定，信使往來之始，瘡痍方深，敝蠹紛然，機彌縫裨讚甚多。

translations.literal: When weapons had just been stilled and envoys were beginning to come and go, wounds were still deep and abuses swarmed; Ji mended and assisted in very many ways.
translations.idiomatic: War had only just ended and diplomatic exchanges were just resuming. The realm was deeply wounded and abuses abounded. Lou Ji contributed greatly to repairing the damage.

sentences.zh: 尤惜名器，守法度；

translations.literal: He especially cherished titles and offices and observed laws and standards;
translations.idiomatic: He was especially careful with offices and titles and upheld law and regulation;

sentences.zh: 進退人物，直言可否，不市私恩，不避嫌怨。

translations.literal: in advancing and retiring men he spoke plainly whether a thing was feasible or not, did not trade in private favors, and did not avoid enmity or resentment.
translations.idiomatic: in promoting or dismissing officials he spoke plainly on what was right, traded in no private favors, and shrank from no enmity.

sentences.zh: 有舉員及格，當改秩作邑而必欲朝闕，機曰：“若是則有勞者何以勸？

translations.literal: There was a candidate who met the standard and ought to change rank to serve as magistrate of a district but insisted on an audience at court; Ji said: "If it is thus, how are those with merit to be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: A candidate who had passed the examination and was due for promotion to district magistrate insisted on an audience at court instead. Lou Ji said, "If that is allowed, how will merit be rewarded?

sentences.zh: 孤寒者何以伸？

translations.literal: How are the isolated and poor to be extended?
translations.idiomatic: How will the poor and obscure advance?

sentences.zh: 若至上前，自應執奏。

translations.literal: If he comes before the sovereign, he should himself memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: If he wishes to appeal to the throne, let him submit a memorial himself.

sentences.zh: ”堂吏寄資未仕，而例以升朝官賞陳乞封贈，機曰：“進士非通籍不能及親，汝輩乃以白身得之耶？

translations.literal: " A bureau clerk had registered capital but had not yet taken office, yet by precedent sought enfeoffment and posthumous honors as a court-presenting official; Ji said: "A jinshi cannot reach his parents unless he is entered in the registers—do you people obtain it as plain commoners?
translations.idiomatic: " A bureau clerk who had registered capital but had not yet taken office sought posthumous honors for his parents under the precedent for court-presenting officials. Lou Ji said, "A jinshi cannot honor his parents until he holds office. Do you think you can obtain such honors as private citizens?

sentences.zh: ”嘉定二年八月，行皇太子冊命，機攝中書令讀冊。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month of the second year of Jiading the investiture of the heir apparent was performed; Ji acted as director of the Secretariat and read the patent.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth month of the second year of Jiading (1209), when the crown prince's investiture was performed, Lou Ji acted as director of the Secretariat and read the patent of appointment.

sentences.zh: 九月祀明堂，為禮儀使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he sacrificed at the Bright Hall and served as ritual commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, when sacrifices were offered at the Bright Hall, he served as ritual commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數上章告老，帝不許，皇太子遣官屬勉留之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials requesting retirement; the emperor did not permit it; the heir apparent sent officials to urge him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly requested retirement, but the emperor refused. The crown prince sent officials to urge him to stay.

sentences.zh: 以資政殿學士知福州，力辭。

translations.literal: He was made academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and magistrate of Fuzhou, and strenuously declined.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and magistrate of Fuzhou, he declined firmly.

sentences.zh: 提舉洞霄宮以歸，遂卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，加贈特進。

translations.literal: He was made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace and returned home, then died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with additional posthumous promotion to Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace, he returned home and soon died. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with an additional posthumous promotion to Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 機初登第，其父壽戒之曰：“得官誠可喜，然為官正自未易爾！

translations.literal: When Ji first passed the examination, his father Shou admonished him, saying: "Obtaining office is truly a joy, yet being an official is in itself not easy!
translations.idiomatic: When Lou Ji first passed the examinations, his father Shou admonished him, saying, "Gaining office is indeed a joy, but serving as an official is not easy!

sentences.zh: ”機撫其弟模、棟，卒為善士。

translations.literal: " Ji reared his younger brothers Mo and Dong, who in the end became good men.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised his younger brothers Mo and Dong, who both became men of virtue.

sentences.zh: 居鄉以誠接物，是非枉直判於語下，不為後言，人憚而服之。

translations.literal: Living in his home district he met others with sincerity; right and wrong, crooked and straight, he judged in the moment of speech and did not speak afterward; people feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: At home he dealt with others sincerely. He judged right and wrong on the spot and never spoke behind people's backs. Others feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 稱獎人才，不遺寸長，訪問賢能，疏列姓名及其可用之實，以備采取，其所薦進，亦不欲人之知也。

translations.literal: He praised and commended talent, omitting no small merit; he inquired after the worthy and able, listed their names in memorials with the facts of their usability for selection, and those he recommended for advancement he also did not wish others to know.
translations.idiomatic: He praised talent and overlooked no small merit. He sought out the worthy and able, listed their names in memorials with notes on how they might serve, and did not wish others to know whom he had recommended.

sentences.zh: 所著復有《班馬字類》。

translations.literal: Among his writings there was also the "Classified Characters of Ban and Sima."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the "Classified Characters of Ban and Sima."

sentences.zh: 機深於書學，尺牘人多藏弆雲。

translations.literal: Ji was deep in the study of writing; many people treasured his letters, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ji was deeply learned in calligraphy, and many people treasured his letters.

sentences.zh: 沈煥，字叔晦，定海人。

translations.literal: Shen Huan, style name Shuhui, was a man of Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huan, whose style name was Shuhui, came from Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 試入太學，始與臨川陸九齡為友，從而學焉。

translations.literal: On trial entry into the Imperial Academy, he first befriended Lu Jiuling of Linchuan and followed him in study.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the Imperial Academy he first befriended Lu Jiuling of Linchuan and studied under him.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年舉進士，授餘姚尉、揚州教授。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiandao he was presented as jinshi and appointed assistant magistrate of Yuyao and professor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Qiandao (1169) and was appointed assistant magistrate of Yuyao and professor at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為太學錄，以所躬行者淑諸人，蚤暮延見學者，孜孜誨誘，長貳同僚忌其立異。

translations.literal: He was summoned as recorder of the Imperial Academy; with what he personally practiced he purified others, morning and evening receiving and seeing students, diligently instructing and guiding; the senior and second officials and colleagues resented his standing apart.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to serve as recorder of the Imperial Academy, he taught by personal example, received students morning and evening, and instructed them tirelessly. Senior officials and colleagues resented his unconventional ways.

sentences.zh: 會充殿試考官，唱名日序立庭下，帝偉其儀觀，遣內侍問姓名，眾滋忌之。

translations.literal: When he served as examiner of the palace examination, on the day names were announced he stood in order in the courtyard; the emperor admired his bearing and appearance and sent an inner attendant to ask his name; the crowd grew ever more jealous.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as an examiner of the palace examination, on the day candidates were announced he stood in the courtyard in formal order. The emperor admired his bearing and sent a palace attendant to ask his name. His colleagues grew even more jealous.

sentences.zh: 或勸其姑營職，道未可行也，煥曰：“道與職有二乎？

translations.literal: Some urged him for the time being to pursue office, saying the Way could not yet be practiced; Huan said: "Are the Way and office two different things?
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to focus on advancing his career, saying the Way could not yet be put into practice. Shen Huan replied, "Are the Way and one's office two different things?

sentences.zh: ”適私試發策，引《孟子》：“立乎人之本朝而道不行，恥也。

translations.literal: " Just then in a private examination he set a policy question, citing the "Mencius": "To stand in the court of one's lord and have the Way not practiced—this is shame."
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward, in setting a policy question for a private examination, he quoted the "Mencius": "To stand in one's ruler's court while the Way goes unheeded is shameful."

sentences.zh: ”言路以為訕己，請黜之，在職才八旬，調高郵軍教授而去。

translations.literal: " The remonstrance officials took this as mocking themselves and requested his dismissal; he had been in office only eighty days when he was transferred to be professor of Gaoyou Commandery and left.
translations.idiomatic: " The remonstrance officials took this as a personal insult and requested his dismissal. After only eighty days in office he was transferred to serve as professor at Gaoyou Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後充幹辦浙東安撫司公事。

translations.literal: Later he served as staff officer of the Zhedong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as a staff officer on the Zhedong Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 高宗山陵，百司次舍供帳酒食之需，供給不暇，煥亟言於安撫使鄭汝諧曰：“國有大戚，而臣子宴樂自如，安乎？

translations.literal: At the mountain tomb of Gaozong, the hundred offices' temporary lodgings required provisions, tents, wine, and food, and supplies could not keep up; Huan urgently spoke to the pacification commissioner Zheng Ruhe, saying: "The state has a great grief, yet ministers feast and make merry as usual—is this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: During the construction of Gaozong's mausoleum, the temporary quarters of the various offices required endless supplies of food and wine. Shen Huan urgently told the pacification commissioner Zheng Ruhe, "The state is in deep mourning, yet officials feast and make merry as usual. How can that be right?

sentences.zh: ”汝諧屬煥條奏。

translations.literal: " Ruhe entrusted Huan to set forth the matter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Ruhe had Shen Huan draft a memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 充修奉官，移書御史，請明示喪紀本意，使貴近哀戚之心重，則茇舍菲食自安，不煩彈劾而須索絕矣。

translations.literal: Serving as maintenance officer, he sent a letter to the censorate requesting clear exposition of the original intent of mourning regulations, so that the noble and near would weigh grief heavily; then crude shelters and plain food would be accepted of themselves, and there would be no need for impeachment while demands and exactions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: As a maintenance officer he wrote to the censorate asking that the true meaning of mourning regulations be made clear, so that high officials would take grief seriously. Then crude quarters and plain food would suffice, and there would be no need for impeachment or endless demands.

sentences.zh: 於是治並緣為奸者，追償率斂者，支費頓減。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who used the occasion to commit wrongdoing were punished, those who pursued repayment and extortion were pursued for compensation, and expenditures abruptly decreased.
translations.idiomatic: Those who used the occasion to commit fraud were punished, extortionists were made to repay what they had taken, and expenditures dropped sharply.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，常平使分擇官屬振恤，得上虞、餘姚二縣，無復流殍。

translations.literal: In a year of drought the Ever-Normal intendant selected officials to distribute relief; he obtained Shangyu and Yuyao counties, and there were no more corpses of the destitute drifting about.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year the Ever-Normal intendant selected officials to distribute relief. Shen Huan was assigned Shangyu and Yuyao counties, and no more corpses of the destitute were seen drifting about.

sentences.zh: 改知婺源，三省類薦書以聞，遂通判舒州。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Wuyuan; the three departments repeatedly submitted recommendation letters to inform the throne, and he then became vice-prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to serve as magistrate of Wuyuan, he was repeatedly recommended by the three departments and was then appointed vice-prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 閑居雖病，猶不廢讀書，拳拳然以母老為念、善類凋零為憂。

translations.literal: Living in retirement though ill, he still did not abandon reading, earnestly mindful of his aged mother and grieved that good men were withering away.
translations.idiomatic: Though ill in retirement, he never stopped reading. He was deeply mindful of his aged mother and grieved that worthy men were dying off.

sentences.zh: 卒，丞相周必大聞之曰：“追思立朝不能推賢揚善，予愧叔晦，益者三友，叔晦不予愧也。”

translations.literal: He died; the chief councilor Zhou Bida, hearing of it, said: "Looking back on my time at court, I could not promote the worthy and exalt the good—I am ashamed before Shuhui; of the three friends who benefit one, Shuhui does not shame me.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Chief Councilor Zhou Bida said, "Looking back on my time at court, I failed to promote the worthy and advance the good. I am ashamed before Shuhui. Of the three friends who benefit one, Shuhui is not ashamed of me.

sentences.zh: 煥人品高明，而其中未安，不苟自恕，常曰晝觀諸妻子，夜卜諸夢寐，兩者無愧，始可以言學。

translations.literal: Huan's character was lofty and bright, yet within he was not at ease and did not lightly forgive himself; he often said: by day observe your wife and children, by night consult your dreams—when both are without shame, then one may speak of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huan's character was lofty, yet he was never fully at ease with himself and did not lightly forgive his faults. He often said, "By day observe your wife and children; by night consult your dreams. When both are without shame, only then may one speak of learning."

sentences.zh: 追贈直華文閣，特諡端憲。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion, with the special posthumous title Duanxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and given the special posthumous title Duanxian (Upright and Law-abiding).

sentences.zh: 煥之友舒璘字元質，一字元賓，奉化人。

translations.literal: Huan's friend Shu Lin, style name Yuanzhi, another style name Yuanbin, was a man of Fenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huan's friend Shu Lin, whose style names were Yuanzhi and Yuanbin, came from Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 補入太學。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy by supplement.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy by special admission.

sentences.zh: 張栻官中都，璘往從之，有所開警。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shi held office in the capital, Lin went to follow him and received enlightenment and warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shi served in the capital, Shu Lin went to study with him and received much enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 又從陸九淵遊，曰：“吾惟朝於斯，夕於斯，刻苦磨厲，改過遷善，日有新功，亦可以弗叛矣乎。

translations.literal: He also traveled with Lu Jiuyuan, saying: "I only morning at this and evening at this, grinding myself hard, correcting faults and moving toward goodness, daily having new achievement—may one also not turn away?"
translations.idiomatic: He also studied with Lu Jiuyuan, saying, "If I devote myself morning and evening, strive diligently, correct my faults, move toward goodness, and make new progress each day, may I not then remain faithful to the Way?"

sentences.zh: ”朱熹、呂祖謙講學於婺，璘徒步往謁之，以書告其家曰：“敝床疏席，總是佳趣；

translations.literal: " Zhu Xi and Lü Zuqian lectured in Wu; Lin went on foot to visit them, and wrote to his family, saying: "A worn bed and plain mat are altogether fine pleasures;
translations.idiomatic: " When Zhu Xi and Lü Zuqian were teaching in Wu, Shu Lin walked there to visit them. He wrote home, saying, "A worn bed and plain mat are pleasures enough;

sentences.zh: 櫛風沐雨，反為美境。”

translations.literal: wind-combed and rain-bathed, on the contrary become a beautiful realm.
translations.idiomatic: to brave wind and rain is itself a beautiful realm."

sentences.zh: 舉乾道八年進士，兩授郡教授，不赴。

translations.literal: He was presented as jinshi in the eighth year of Qiandao; twice appointed prefectural professor, he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Qiandao (1172). Twice appointed prefectural professor, he declined both times.

sentences.zh: 繼為江西轉運司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: He next served as staff officer of the Jiangxi Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He next served as a staff officer on the Jiangxi Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 或忌璘所學，望風心議，及與璘處，了無疑間。

translations.literal: Some resented Lin's learning and at a distance harbored criticism in their hearts, but once they were with Lin there was not the slightest doubt or estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Some resented his scholarship and criticized him from afar, but once they met him they harbored no suspicion at all.

sentences.zh: 為微州教授，微習頓異。

translations.literal: He served as professor of Huizhou, and Huizhou customs abruptly changed.
translations.idiomatic: As professor at Huizhou, he quickly transformed local scholarly customs.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《禮》久不預貢士，學幾無傳，璘作《詩禮講解》，家傳人習，自是其學浸盛。

translations.literal: The "Odes" and "Rites" had long not been included among presented scholars, and learning was nearly without transmission; Lin composed "Explanations of the Odes and Rites," which families transmitted and people studied, and from then on his learning gradually flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The "Odes" and "Rites" had long been omitted from the examination curriculum, and the tradition was nearly lost. Shu Lin wrote "Explanations of the Odes and Rites," which families passed down and students studied. From then on his school gradually flourished.

sentences.zh: 丞相留正稱璘為當今第一教官，司業汪逵首欲薦璘，或謂璘舉員已足，逵曰：“吾職當舉教官，舍斯人將誰先？

translations.literal: Chief councilor Liu Zheng called Lin the foremost instructor of the age; vice director Wang Kui was the first to wish to recommend Lin; some said Lin's quota of recommendations was already full; Kui said: "My duty is to recommend instructors—leaving this man aside, whom shall I put first?
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Liu Zheng called Shu Lin the foremost teacher of the age. Vice Director Wang Kui was the first to recommend him. Some said Lin's recommendation quota was already full. Wang Kui replied, "My duty is to recommend teachers. If not this man, whom should I recommend first?

sentences.zh: ”卒剡薦之。

translations.literal: " In the end he submitted a recommendation for him.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he submitted the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 知平陽縣，郡政頗苛，及璘以民病告，辭嚴義正，守為改容。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Pingyang County; prefectural government was rather harsh; when Lin reported the people's afflictions, his words were stern and righteous, and the prefect changed his expression.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Pingyang, he found prefectural policy harsh. When he reported the people's hardships, his words were stern and principled, and the prefect changed his manner.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，通判宜州，卒。

translations.literal: When his term ended he became vice-prefect of Yizhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was appointed vice-prefect of Yizhou, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 璘樂於教人，嚐曰：“師道尊嚴，璘不如叔晦，若啟迪後進，則璘不敢多遜。

translations.literal: Lin delighted in teaching people and once said: "In the dignity of the teacher's Way, Lin is not the equal of Shuhui; but in enlightening later students, Lin does not dare yield much.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Lin loved teaching and once said, "In the dignity of the teacher's Way I am not Shen Huan's equal, but in guiding younger students I would not yield much to anyone.

sentences.zh: ”袁燮謂璘篤實不欺，無豪發矯偽。

translations.literal: " Yuan Xie said Lin was sincere and did not deceive, without the slightest trace of pretense.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Xie said he was sincere and never deceptive, without the slightest pretense.

sentences.zh: 楊簡謂璘孝友忠實，道心融明。

translations.literal: Yang Jian said Lin was filial, friendly, loyal, and sincere, with a luminous and integrated moral mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian said he was filial, friendly, loyal, and sincere, with a luminous moral mind.

sentences.zh: 樓鑰謂璘之於人，如熙然之陽春。

translations.literal: Lou Yue said Lin toward people was like a warm spring sun.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Yue said his effect on people was like a warm spring sun.

sentences.zh: 淳祐中，特諡文靖。

translations.literal: In the Chunyou period he was specially given the posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunyou era he was posthumously given the title Wenjing (Cultured and Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 曹彥約字簡甫，都昌人。

translations.literal: Cao Yanyue, style name Jianfu, was a man of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue, whose style name was Jianfu, came from Duchang.

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eighth year of Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chunxi (1181).

sentences.zh: 嚐從朱熹講學，曆建平尉、桂陽司錄、辰溪令，知樂平縣，主管江西安撫司機宜文字。

translations.literal: He once studied under Zhu Xi in lecture, and successively served as assistant magistrate of Jianping, registrar of Guiyang, magistrate of Chenxi, magistrate of Leping County, and in charge of confidential documents of the Jiangxi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Zhu Xi and served successively as assistant magistrate of Jianping, registrar of Guiyang, magistrate of Chenxi, magistrate of Leping County, and confidential secretary on the Jiangxi Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 知澧州，未上，薛叔似宣撫京湖，辟主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lizhou but had not yet taken up the post when Xue Shusi pacified Jinghu and Hubei and invited him as chief confidential secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Lizhou, he had not yet taken office when Xue Shusi, pacification commissioner of Jinghu and Hubei, invited him to serve as chief confidential secretary.

sentences.zh: 漢陽闕守，檄攝軍事。

translations.literal: Hanyang lacked a magistrate; he was ordered by dispatch to take charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanyang lacked a magistrate, he was ordered by dispatch to take charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時金人大入，郡兵素寡弱，彥約搜訪土豪，得許禼俾總民兵，趙觀俾防水道，黨仲升將宣撫司軍屯郡城。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin entered in force; the prefectural troops had always been few and weak; Yanyue searched out local strongmen, obtained Xu Qi to command the militia, Zhao Guan to defend the waterways, and Dang Zhongsheng to lead the pacification commission troops garrisoned in the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded in force, the prefectural troops were few and weak. Cao Yanyue sought out local leaders, appointed Xu Qi to command the militia, Zhao Guan to defend the waterways, and Dang Zhongsheng to lead the pacification commission troops garrisoned in the city.

sentences.zh: 金重兵圍安陸，遊騎闖漢川，彥約授觀方略，結漁戶拒守南河，觀逆擊，斬其先鋒，且遣死士焚其戰艦，晝夜殊死戰，北渡追擊，金人大敗去。

translations.literal: The Jin with heavy forces besieged Anlu; roaming cavalry broke into Hanchuan; Yanyue gave Guan strategy; he united fishermen to hold the south river, Guan counterattacked and beheaded their vanguard, and also sent death-defying soldiers to burn their warships; day and night they fought to the death; crossing north to pursue, the Jin suffered great defeat and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces in strength besieged Anlu while raiding cavalry broke into Hanchuan. Cao Yanyue gave Zhao Guan his plan: Guan rallied fishermen to defend the south river, counterattacked and beheaded the Jin vanguard, and sent volunteers to burn their warships. After a day-and-night battle he crossed the river in pursuit, and the Jin were routed.

sentences.zh: 又遣仲升劫金人砦，殺千餘人，仲升中流矢死。

translations.literal: He also sent Zhongsheng to raid a Jin camp, killing more than a thousand; Zhongsheng was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Dang Zhongsheng to raid a Jin camp, killing more than a thousand men. Zhongsheng was struck by a stray arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 奏觀補成忠郎、漢川簿尉，贈仲升修武郎，官其後二人。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Guan be supplemented as Gentleman of Loyal Achievement and registrar of Hanchuan, posthumously enfeoffed Zhongsheng as Gentleman of Martial Cultivation, and gave offices to his two descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized rewards for Guan as Gentleman of Loyal Achievement and registrar of Hanchuan, posthumously enfeoffed Zhongsheng as Gentleman of Martial Cultivation, and gave offices to two of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 彥約以守禦功進秩二等，就知漢陽。

translations.literal: Yanyue for his defense merit was advanced two ranks in grade and was appointed magistrate of Hanyang on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: For his defensive merit Cao Yanyue was promoted two ranks and appointed magistrate of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，詔求言，彥約上封事，謂“敵豈不以歲幣為利，惟其所向輒應，所求輒得，以我為易與而縱其欲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading an edict sought opinions; Yanyue submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Would the enemy not take the annual tribute as profit? Whatever they aim at is answered, whatever they seek is obtained—they take us as easy to deal with and indulge their desires.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading (1208) the emperor sought opinions. Cao Yanyue submitted a sealed memorial arguing that the enemy profited from annual tribute because whatever they demanded was granted. They treated Song as easy to manipulate and indulged their desires.

sentences.zh: 莫若遲留小使，督責邊備，假以歲月，當知真偽。

translations.literal: Better to detain the minor envoys, supervise and press border defenses, and allow some months and years—then one will know truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Better to detain the minor envoys, strengthen border defenses, and allow time to reveal their true intentions.

sentences.zh: 設復大舉。

translations.literal: Suppose they again mount a major campaign.
translations.idiomatic: If they launch another major invasion,

sentences.zh: 則民固已怨矣，欲進而我已戒嚴，欲退而彼有叛兵，決勝可期矣。

translations.literal: then the people will already be resentful; if they wish to advance we are already on alert; if they wish to withdraw they have mutinous troops—decisive victory may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: the people will already be resentful. If they advance, we will already be on alert. If they retreat, they may face mutiny. Victory can then be expected.

sentences.zh: ”尋提舉湖北常平，權知鄂州兼湖廣總領，改提點刑獄，遷湖南轉運判官。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he was made intendant of the Hubei Ever-Normal Granary, acting magistrate of Ezhou and concurrently general controller of Huguang, changed to judicial intendant, and moved to transport judge of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was made intendant of the Hubei Ever-Normal Granary, acting magistrate of Ezhou and general controller of Huguang, then judicial intendant, and finally transport judge of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時盜羅世傳、李元礪、李新等相繼竊發，桂陽、茶陵、安仁三縣皆破，環地千里，莽為盜區。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits Luo Shichuan, Li Yuanli, Li Xin, and others rose in succession; Guiyang, Chaling, and Anren counties were all overrun; for a thousand li around the wilds became bandit territory.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits led by Luo Shichuan, Li Yuanli, Li Xin, and others rose in succession. Guiyang, Chaling, and Anren counties were overrun, and a thousand-li region became bandit territory.

sentences.zh: 彥約至攸督運，人心始定。

translations.literal: When Yanyue reached You to supervise transport, popular sentiment first settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Yanyue reached You County to supervise transport, public order was restored.

sentences.zh: 遷直秘閣、知潭州、湖南安撫。

translations.literal: He was moved to direct academician of the Secret Archive, magistrate of Tanzhou, and pacification commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct academician of the Secret Archive, appointed magistrate of Tanzhou, and made pacification commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時江西言欲招安李元礪，朝命下湖南議招討之宜，彥約言：“ 今不行討捕，曲徇招安，失朝廷威重。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangxi proposed wishing to win Li Yuanli over by amnesty; the court ordered Hunan to discuss the propriety of amnesty and suppression; Yanyue said: "If now suppression and pursuit are not carried out but amnesty is bent to indulgently, the court's authority and weight are lost.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi proposed offering amnesty to Li Yuanli. The court ordered Hunan to discuss the policy. Cao Yanyue argued, "If we do not pursue and suppress the bandits but bend to amnesty, we lose the court's authority.

sentences.zh: 若無礪設疑詞以款重兵，則兵不可撤戍，民不得安業。

translations.literal: If Yuanli sets up doubtful words to detain heavy troops, then troops cannot withdraw from garrison and the people cannot settle in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuanli uses delaying tactics to hold our troops in place, the garrisons cannot withdraw and the people cannot return to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: ”元礪果不可降，彥約乃督諸將逼賊巢而屯，擊破李新於酃洣，新中創死，眾推李如鬆為首，如鬆降，遂復桂陽。

translations.literal: " Yuanli indeed could not be made to surrender; Yanyue then supervised the generals in pressing the bandit lair and encamping, defeated Li Xin at Ling and Mi, Xin died of a wound, the crowd made Li Rusong leader, Rusong surrendered, and Guiyang was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanli indeed would not surrender. Cao Yanyue then directed the generals to press the bandit strongholds. Li Xin was defeated at Ling and Mi and died of his wounds. The bandits made Li Rusong their leader; Rusong surrendered, and Guiyang was recovered.

sentences.zh: 世傳素與元礪有隙，至是密請圖元礪以自效，彥約錄賞格報之，且告於朝，又予萬緡錢犒其師。

translations.literal: Shichuan had long had a rift with Yuanli; at this point he secretly requested to plot against Yuanli to prove his merit; Yanyue recorded the reward regulations and replied, and also informed the court, giving ten thousand strings of cash to reward his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shichuan had long been at odds with Yuanli and now secretly offered to capture him. Cao Yanyue recorded the reward regulations, reported to court, and gave ten thousand strings of cash to reward his troops.

sentences.zh: 世傳遂禽元礪。

translations.literal: Shichuan thereupon captured Yuanli.
translations.idiomatic: Shichuan then captured Yuanli.

sentences.zh: 彥約還長沙，未幾，復出督戰，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Yanyue returned to Changsha; before long he again went out to supervise the fighting, and the remaining factions were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue returned to Changsha. Soon afterward he went out again to direct operations, and the remaining bandits were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 世傳既自以為功，遲留以邀重賂，彥約諭以不宜格外邀求。

translations.literal: Shichuan, having taken the merit upon himself, lingered to seek heavy bribes; Yanyue instructed him that he ought not seek extra rewards beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Shichuan, claiming the credit, lingered to demand heavy rewards. Cao Yanyue told him he should not seek excessive payment.

sentences.zh: 時池州副都統許俊駐兵吉之龍泉，厚賂以結世傳，超格許轉官資，世傳遂以元礪解江西。

translations.literal: At that time the vice commander-in-chief of Chizhou Xu Jun was garrisoned at Longquan in Ji, gave heavy bribes to win Shichuan, and beyond regulations promised transfer of official rank; Shichuan then delivered Yuanli to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jun, vice commander-in-chief of Chizhou, was stationed at Longquan in Ji. He bribed Shichuan heavily and promised him promotion beyond regulations. Shichuan then handed Yuanli over to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 胡榘為右司，欲以世傳盡統諸峒而為之帥，悉徹江西、湖南戍兵，彥約固爭之，榘不悅，然世傳終桀驁不肯出峒。

translations.literal: Hu Ju was right bureau director and wished to have Shichuan command all the mountain stockades and make him their commander, entirely withdrawing the garrison troops of Jiangxi and Hunan; Yanyue firmly contested this; Ju was displeased, yet Shichuan in the end was arrogant and obstinate and would not leave the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ju of the right bureau wished to put Shichuan in command of all the mountain stockades and withdraw all Jiangxi and Hunan garrisons. Cao Yanyue strongly opposed this. Hu was displeased, but Shichuan remained arrogant and refused to leave the mountains.

sentences.zh: 彥約密遣羅九遷為間，誘胡友睦，許以重賞，友睦遂殺世傳。

translations.literal: Yanyue secretly sent Luo Jiuqian as an agent to entice Hu Youmu, promising heavy reward; Youmu thereupon killed Shichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue secretly sent Luo Jiuqian as an agent to entice Hu Youmu with a heavy reward. Youmu then killed Shichuan.

sentences.zh: 江西來爭功，不與校。

translations.literal: Jiangxi came to dispute merit; he did not contend with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi disputed the credit, he did not argue with them.

sentences.zh: 擢侍右郎官，以右正言鄭昭先言，寢其命。

translations.literal: He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary; because right rectifier Zheng Zhao spoke first, the appointment was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary, but Right Rectifier Zheng Zhao objected and the appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 久之，以為利路轉運判官兼知利州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made transport judge of Lizhou Road and concurrently magistrate of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed transport judge of Lizhou Road and concurrently magistrate of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 關外乏食，彥約悉發本司所儲減價遣糶，勸分免役，通商蠲稅，民賴以濟。

translations.literal: Outside the passes food was scarce; Yanyue fully released what his commission stored and sent it out for sale at reduced price, urged sharing and exemption from corvée, opened trade and remitted taxes, and the people relied on this to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Food was scarce beyond the passes. Cao Yanyue released all stored grain for sale at reduced prices, urged mutual aid and corvée exemptions, opened trade, and remitted taxes. The people were thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 時沔州都統製王大才驕橫，製置使董居誼既不得其柄，反曲意奉之。

translations.literal: At that time the commander-in-chief of Mianzhou Wang Dacai was arrogant and overbearing; the commissioner Dong Juyi, having failed to obtain control, on the contrary bent his will to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dacai, commander-in-chief of Mianzhou, was arrogant and overbearing. Commissioner Dong Juyi, unable to control him, instead flattered him.

sentences.zh: 彥約以蜀之邊麵諸司並列，兵權不一，微有小警，紛然奏議，理財者歸怨於兵弱，握兵者歸咎於財寡，乃作《病夫議》，獻之廟堂，曰：

translations.literal: Yanyue, because on the Sichuan frontier the various commissions stood side by side and military authority was not unified, when there was even a slight alarm memorials flew in confusion; those managing finances blamed weak troops, those holding troops blamed scant funds—he therefore composed "Discourse of the Sick Man," presented it to the court, and said:
translations.idiomatic: Because on the Sichuan frontier the various commissions stood side by side and military authority was divided, even a minor alarm produced a flood of conflicting memorials. Finance officials blamed weak troops; military commanders blamed scant funds. Cao Yanyue therefore wrote "Discourse of the Sick Man" and presented it to court, saying:

sentences.zh: 古之臨邊，求一賢者而盡付之兵權，兵權正則事體重，兵權專則號令一。

translations.literal: In antiquity on the frontier, one sought a single worthy man and entrusted him fully with military authority; when military authority was correct the matter was weighty, when military authority was concentrated commands were unified.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity on the frontier, one sought a single worthy man and entrusted him fully with military authority. When authority was properly vested the matter was weighty; when it was concentrated commands were unified.

sentences.zh: 今廟堂之上，患士大夫不奉行詔令，惡士大夫不恪守忠實。

translations.literal: Now above in the court hall, the worry is that scholar-officials do not carry out edicts and commands, and the hatred is that scholar-officials do not strictly keep loyalty and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Today at court the worry is that officials do not carry out edicts, and the fear is that they do not remain loyal and sincere.

sentences.zh: 故雖信而用之，又以人參之；

translations.literal: Therefore though one trusts and employs him, one also has others participate;
translations.idiomatic: So though one trusts and employs a man, one also sets others to supervise him;

sentences.zh: 雖以事權付之，又從中禦以係維之。

translations.literal: though one entrusts him with authority over affairs, one again controls him from the center to tie and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: and though one entrusts him with authority, one still controls him from the center to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 致使知事者不敢任事，畏事者常至失事，卒有緩急，各持己見，兵權財計，互相歸咎。

translations.literal: This causes those who know affairs not to dare undertake them, and those who fear affairs often to fail in them; when finally there is urgency, each holds his own view, and military authority and financial planning blame one another.
translations.idiomatic: This makes capable men afraid to act and timid men prone to failure. When crisis comes, each clings to his own view, and military and financial officials blame one another.

sentences.zh: 昔秦、隴之俗，以知兵善戰聞天下。

translations.literal: Formerly the customs of Qin and Long were renowned throughout the realm for knowing warfare and being skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the people of Qin and Long were renowned throughout the realm for military skill.

sentences.zh: 自吳氏世襲以來，握兵者誌在於怙勢，不在於尊上；

translations.literal: Since the Wu family's hereditary succession, those who held troops aimed at relying on power, not at honoring superiors;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wu family's hereditary rule, those who held troops aimed to rely on power, not to honor superiors;

sentences.zh: 用兵者誌在於誅貨，不在於息民。

translations.literal: those who used troops aimed at seeking goods by force, not at giving the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: and those who used troops aimed to seize wealth, not to give the people rest.

sentences.zh: 本原一壞，百病間出，至有世將已叛而宣威不覺，四郡已割而諸將不知。

translations.literal: Once the root was ruined, a hundred ailments issued forth one after another, reaching the point that a hereditary general had already rebelled while the Pacification Commissioner did not notice, and four prefectures had already been carved away while the generals did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Once the root was corrupted, countless ills followed. A hereditary general had rebelled while the pacification commissioner did not notice; four prefectures had been lost while the generals remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 更化之後，逆黨既誅，而土俗人心其實未改。

translations.literal: After the change of policy, the rebellious faction was already executed, yet local custom and popular hearts in truth had not changed.
translations.idiomatic: After the policy change the rebels were executed, yet local customs and popular attitudes had not truly changed.

sentences.zh: 任軍官而領州事者，易成藩鎮之權；

translations.literal: Those who were military officers yet led prefectural affairs easily formed the power of separatist domains;
translations.idiomatic: Military officers who also governed prefectures easily became regional warlords;

sentences.zh: 起行伍而立微效者，漸無階級之分。

translations.literal: those who rose from the ranks and achieved slight merit gradually lost distinction of grade.
translations.idiomatic: and men who rose from the ranks with slight merit gradually lost proper rank distinctions.

sentences.zh: 由皂郊以至宕昌，即隴西天水之地，其忠義民兵利在戰鬥，緩急之際固易鼓率，若其恃勇貪利，犯上作亂，則又不止於大軍而已。

translations.literal: From Zaojiao to Dangchang, which is the land of Longxi and Tianshui, their loyal and righteous militia profit in fighting; in moments of urgency they are indeed easy to rouse and lead—yet if they rely on courage and covet profit, offend superiors and make rebellion, then the harm is not limited to the great armies alone.
translations.idiomatic: From Zaojiao to Dangchang—the region of Longxi and Tianshui—the loyal militia profit from fighting and are easy to rally in emergencies. But if they rely on courage, covet profit, offend superiors, and rebel, the harm extends far beyond the regular armies.

sentences.zh: 苟不正其本原，磨之以歲月，漸之以禮義，未見其可也。

translations.literal: If one does not correct the root, grind it with years and months, and gradually apply ritual and righteousness, one does not see how it can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the root is corrected, shaped over years, and gradually guided by ritual and righteousness, success is unlikely.

sentences.zh: 今日之領帥權者，必當近邊境，必當擁親兵；

translations.literal: Today's commanders with authority must be stationed near the border and must possess personal troops;
translations.idiomatic: Today's frontier commanders must be stationed on the border and must command personal troops;

sentences.zh: 有兵權者，必當領經費，必當寬用度。

translations.literal: those with military authority must also control funds and must have liberal expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: and those with military authority must control funds and have liberal budgets.

sentences.zh: 至於忠義之兵，又須有德者以為統率，擇知書者以為教導，如古人所謂教民而後用之也。

translations.literal: As for loyal and righteous troops, there must also be men of virtue to command them and learned men chosen to instruct them, as the ancients said of teaching the people and afterward employing them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the loyal militia, men of virtue must command them and learned men must instruct them, as the ancients said: teach the people before employing them in war.

sentences.zh: 今議不出此，乃欲幸勝以為功，苟安以求免，誤天下者必此人也。

translations.literal: Today's deliberations do not proceed from this; they only wish to take lucky victory as merit and seek ease to escape blame—the one who will mislead the realm must be this kind of man.
translations.idiomatic: Today's policy does not follow this course. Officials seek lucky victories and easy escapes from blame. The man who will mislead the realm is such a one.

sentences.zh: 時朝論未以為然。

translations.literal: At the time court opinion did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion at the time did not agree.

sentences.zh: 差知寧國府，又改知隆興府、江西安撫。

translations.literal: He was assigned to know Ningguo Prefecture, then changed to know Longxing Prefecture and pacification commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned magistrate of Ningguo Prefecture, he was then transferred to Longxing Prefecture and made pacification commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 居亡何，蜀邊被兵，內有張福、莫簡之變，彥約之言無一不驗。

translations.literal: Before long the Sichuan frontier suffered warfare, and within there was the disturbance of Zhang Fu and Mo Jian; not one of Yanyue's words failed to prove true.
translations.idiomatic: Before long warfare struck the Sichuan frontier and the Zhang Fu and Mo Jian mutiny broke out within the province. Every warning Cao Yanyue had given proved true.

sentences.zh: 遷大理少卿，又權戶部侍郎，以寶謨閣待制知成都。

translations.literal: He was moved to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, also acting vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and as designated drafter of the Baomo Pavilion was magistrate of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and acting vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, he was made designated drafter of the Baomo Pavilion and magistrate of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 彥約乞赴闕奏事，不允，又申省乞入對，不報。

translations.literal: Yanyue requested to go to court to memorialize on affairs; it was not granted; he again petitioned the Secretariat requesting an audience; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue asked to go to court to report on affairs but was refused. He petitioned the Secretariat for an audience but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 改知福州，又改知潭州，彥約力辭，提舉明道觀，尋以煥章閣待制提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Fuzhou, then again to magistrate of Tanzhou; Yanyue strenuously declined; he was made intendant of the Mingdao Abbey, and shortly afterward as designated drafter of the Huanzhang Pavilion intendant of the Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Fuzhou and then Tanzhou, he declined firmly and was made intendant of the Mingdao Abbey. Soon afterward he was made designated drafter of the Huanzhang Pavilion and intendant of the Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，擢兵部侍郎兼國史院同修撰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, he was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of War and concurrent reviser of the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong ascended the throne, he was promoted to vice minister of war and concurrent reviser of the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年入對，勸帝講學，防近習。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoqing he had an audience and urged the emperor to pursue learning and guard against intimate attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoqing (1225) he had an audience and urged the emperor to pursue learning and guard against intimate attendants.

sentences.zh: 次言：“當以慶曆、元祐聽言為法，以紹聖、崇、觀諱言為戒。

translations.literal: He next said: "One should take Qingli and Yuanyou listening to words as the model, and take Shaosheng, Chongning, and Guanning taboo on words as the warning.
translations.idiomatic: He next said, "Take the openness of the Qingli and Yuanyou eras as your model, and the silencing of dissent in the Shaosheng, Chongning, and Guanning eras as your warning.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，有以賣直好名之說見於奏對者，願陛下倚忠直如蓍龜，去邪佞若蟊賊，其有沮撓讜言者，必加斥逐。”

translations.literal: In recent years there have been those who in memorial audiences put forward the theory of selling uprightness to seek fame; I wish Your Majesty would rely on the loyal and upright as on divining tortoise and milfoil, remove the wicked and flatterers as one removes crop pests, and where there are those who obstruct straightforward speech, surely add reprimand and expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years some have accused honest remonstrators of seeking fame. I urge Your Majesty to rely on the loyal and upright as on divination, remove the wicked and flattering as crop pests, and expel anyone who obstructs honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 會下詔求言，彥約上封事曰：“陛下謹定省以事長樂，開王社以篤天倫，孝友之行，宜足以取信於天下。

translations.literal: When an edict was issued seeking opinions, Yanyue submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Your Majesty carefully attends the inner quarters to serve the Empress Dowager of Eternal Joy, opens the royal altar to deepen heavenly kinship—the conduct of filial piety and brotherly affection ought to be enough to win trust throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict sought opinions, Cao Yanyue submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Your Majesty carefully attends the inner quarters to serve the Empress Dowager, opens the royal altar to deepen family bonds. Your filial and brotherly conduct ought to win trust throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 然兄弟至親，猶誤於狂妄小人之手，道路異說，猶襲於尺布不縫之謠。

translations.literal: Yet brothers most intimate are still misled by the hands of arrogant petty men; strange talk on the roads still follows the rumor of a foot of cloth that will not be sewn together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even between closest brothers, rumors spread by arrogant petty men persist, and the old tale of brothers who could not share a foot of cloth still circulates on the roads.

sentences.zh: 臣以為守法者，人臣之職也，施恩者，人主之柄也。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that observing the law is the duty of a minister, while bestowing grace is the prerogative of the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that observing the law is a minister's duty, while bestowing grace is the sovereign's prerogative.

sentences.zh: 漢淮南王欲危社稷，張蒼、馮敬等請論如法，文帝既赦其罪廢徙，王不幸而死，封其二子於故地。

translations.literal: In Han the King of Huainan wished to endanger the altars of soil and grain; Zhang Cang, Feng Jing, and others requested judgment according to law; Emperor Wen had already pardoned his crime and banished him; the king unfortunately died; he enfeoffed his two sons in their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Huainan of Han threatened the state, Zhang Cang and Feng Jing urged judgment by law. Emperor Wen pardoned him and banished him. When the king died, Wen enfeoffed his two sons in their former lands.

sentences.zh: 此往事之明驗，本朝太宗皇帝之所已行也。

translations.literal: This is a clear proof from past events and what Emperor Taizong of this dynasty has already practiced.
translations.idiomatic: This is a clear precedent from history and a practice already followed by Emperor Taizong of our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 今若徇文帝緣情之義，法太宗繼絕之意，明示好惡，無隙可指，雖不止謗而謗息矣。

translations.literal: If now one follows Emperor Wen's principle of bending to feeling, models Emperor Taizong's intent of continuing severed lines, clearly shows likes and dislikes so that no gap can be pointed to, then though one does not stop slander, slander will cease.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now follows Emperor Wen's humane mercy and Emperor Taizong's intent to continue severed lines, clearly shows your preferences so that no opening remains for slander, slander will cease even without direct suppression.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“陛下求言之詔，惟恐不逮，然外議致疑，以為明言文武，似或止於搢紳，泛言小大，恐不及於韋布，引而伸之，特在一命令之間耳。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Your Majesty's edict seeking words fears only that it does not reach far enough, yet outside opinion raises doubt, thinking that when clearly speaking of civil and military matters it seems perhaps to stop at the gentry and officials, and when broadly speaking of great and small it fears not reaching the common cloth—extending and expanding it depends only on a single command.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Your edict seeking opinions fears only that it does not reach far enough, yet outsiders doubt whether civil and military officials alone are meant, and whether commoners in plain cloth are truly included. Whether that is so depends on a single command from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: ”又薦隆州布衣李心傳素精史學，乞官以初品，置之史館，從之。

translations.literal: " He also recommended the commoner of Longzhou Li Xinchuan, who from of old was skilled in historical learning, requesting an initial-rank office and placement in the History Institute; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " He also recommended Li Xinchuan, a commoner of Longzhou skilled in historical learning, for an initial office in the History Institute. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋兼侍讀，俄遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he held concurrently the post of lecturer, and soon was moved to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served concurrently as lecturer and was soon promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 加寶謨閣直學士，提舉佑神觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was given the direct academician title of the Baomo Pavilion and made intendant of the Youshen Abbey while holding concurrently the lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: Made direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion, he was appointed intendant of the Youshen Abbey while retaining his lectureship.

sentences.zh: 授兵部尚書，力辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of war and strenuously declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed minister of war, he declined firmly and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 改寶章閣學士、知常德府，陛辭，言下情未通，橫斂未革。

translations.literal: He was changed to academician of the Baozhang Pavilion and magistrate of Changde Prefecture; at court farewell he said popular sentiment below was not communicated and harsh exactions were not reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to academician of the Baozhang Pavilion and magistrate of Changde Prefecture, at his farewell audience he said popular sentiment did not reach the throne and harsh exactions had not been reformed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“其病安在？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Where lies the ailment?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Where lies the problem?

sentences.zh: ”對曰：“台諫專言人主，不及時政，下情安得通？

translations.literal: " He replied: "The remonstrators and censors speak only of the sovereign and do not reach current policy—how can sentiment below get through?
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Censors and remonstrators speak only of the sovereign and not of current policy. How can popular sentiment reach the throne?

sentences.zh: 包苴公行於都城，則州郡橫斂，無可疑者。

translations.literal: When gift-wrapped bribes are openly practiced in the capital, then prefectures and districts practice harsh levies—there is no doubt of it.
translations.idiomatic: When bribery is openly practiced in the capital, harsh levies in the provinces are inevitable.

sentences.zh: ”提舉崇福宮，卒，以華文閣學士轉通議大夫致仕，贈宣奉大夫。

translations.literal: " He was made intendant of the Chongfu Palace, died, was transferred as academician of the Huawen Pavilion to Grand Master of Court Discussion for retirement, and posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Court Submission.
translations.idiomatic: " Made intendant of the Chongfu Palace, he soon died. He was granted retirement as academician of the Huawen Pavilion with the rank Grand Master of Court Discussion and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Court Submission.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙初，賜諡文簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiaxi he was given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiaxi era he was posthumously given the title Wenjian (Cultured and Concise).

sentences.zh: 範應鈴，字旂叟，豐城人。

translations.literal: Fan Yingling, style name Qisou, was a man of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yingling, whose style name was Qisou, came from Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 方娠，大父夢雙日照庭，應鈴生。

translations.literal: While still in the womb, his grandfather dreamed of two suns shining on the courtyard; Yingling was born.
translations.idiomatic: While his mother was pregnant, his grandfather dreamed of two suns shining on the courtyard. Yingling was then born.

sentences.zh: 稍長，厲誌於學，丞相周必大見其文，嘉賞之。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older he steeled his will in learning; Chief Councilor Zhou Bida saw his writings and commended them.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he devoted himself zealously to learning. Chief Councilor Zhou Bida read his writings and praised them highly.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，舉進士，調永新尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaixi he was presented as jinshi and was transferred to be assistant magistrate of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaixi (1205) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 縣當龍泉、茶陵溪峒之衝，寇甫平，喜亂者詐為驚擾，應鈴廉得主名，捽而治之。

translations.literal: The county lay on the route of the Longquan and Chaling mountain stockades; bandits had just been pacified, and those who delighted in disorder feigned alarm and disturbance; Yingling with integrity obtained the chief names, seized them, and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay on the route of the Longquan and Chaling stockades. Bandits had just been pacified, yet troublemakers feigned disturbances. Yingling identified the ringleaders, arrested them, and punished them.

sentences.zh: 縣十三鄉，寇擾者不時，安撫使移司兼郡，初奏弛八鄉民租二年，詔下如章。

translations.literal: The county had thirteen townships; bandit disturbances occurred from time to time. The pacification commissioner moved his office and concurrently held the prefecture. He initially memorialized to remit the people’s grain rent in eight townships for two years; an edict was issued as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The county comprised thirteen townships and suffered bandit raids at irregular intervals.
