The pacification commissioner transferred his office and took charge of the prefecture as well. He first memorialized to remit grain rent for two years in eight townships, and an edict was issued accordingly.

sentences.zh: 既而復催以檢核之數，應鈴力爭，不從。

translations.literal: Subsequently they again pressed collection according to verification figures. Yingling strove to argue against it but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, however, officials again demanded payment according to audited quotas. Yingling argued strenuously but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 即詣郡自言，反覆數四，帥聲色俱厲，慶鈴從容曰：“某非徒為八鄉貧民，乃深為州家耳！

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to the prefecture to speak on his own behalf, arguing back and forth four or five times. The intendant’s voice and countenance were both harsh. Yingling said calmly: “I am not merely acting for the poor people of the eight townships — I am deeply acting for the benefit of the prefectural government as well!
translations.idiomatic: He went at once to the prefectural seat to plead the case himself, arguing back and forth several times. The intendant’s voice and expression were both stern. Yingling replied calmly, “I am not pleading only for the poor of those eight townships — I am doing what is best for the prefecture itself!

sentences.zh: 民貧迫之急，將以不肖之心應之，租不可得而禍未易弭也。

translations.literal: When the people are poor and pressed urgently, they will respond with unworthy hearts; rent cannot be obtained and calamities will not be easily quelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the poor are driven to desperation, they will answer with resentment. You will not collect the rent, and the trouble will not easily be stilled.

sentences.zh: ”帥色動，令免下戶。

translations.literal: ” The intendant’s expression changed, and he ordered exemption for lower households.
translations.idiomatic: ” The intendant’s face softened, and he ordered relief for lower-grade households.

sentences.zh: 既出令，復征之，應鈴歎曰：“是使我重失信於民也。

translations.literal: After the order was issued, taxes were again levied. Yingling sighed: “This makes me break faith with the people a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order had been issued, collection was resumed. Yingling sighed, “This forces me to betray the people’s trust all over again.

sentences.zh: ”又力爭之，訖得請，民大感悅。

translations.literal: ” He again strove to argue, and in the end obtained approval; the people were greatly moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: ” He argued again with all his strength and finally won his point. The people were deeply grateful and delighted.

sentences.zh: 有大姓與轉運使有連，家僮恣橫厲民，應鈴笞而係之獄。

translations.literal: A powerful clan had connections with the transport commissioner; their household servants acted arbitrarily and oppressed the people. Yingling whipped them and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: A great family had ties to the transport commissioner, and its servants bullied the people at will. Yingling had them flogged and thrown into jail.

sentences.zh: 郡吏庭辱令，應鈴執吏囚之，以狀聞。

translations.literal: A prefectural clerk publicly humiliated the magistrate in court. Yingling seized the clerk and imprisoned him, reporting the matter upward.
translations.idiomatic: A prefectural clerk publicly insulted the magistrate in court. Yingling arrested the clerk, put him in prison, and reported the affair to higher authorities.

sentences.zh: 調衡州錄事，總領聞應鈴名，辟為屬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be recorder of Hengzhou. The general fiscal supervisor heard of Yingling’s reputation and recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to serve as recorder of Hengzhou, he came to the attention of the general fiscal supervisor, who recruited him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 改知崇仁縣，始至，明約束，信期會，正紀綱，曉諭吏民，使知所趨避。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as magistrate of Chongren County. Upon first arriving, he clarified regulations, honored deadlines, rectified discipline, and instructed officials and people so they would know what to pursue and avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned as magistrate of Chongren County, he made clear the rules on arrival, kept deadlines faithfully, restored order, and instructed officials and commoners alike in what to follow and what to shun.

sentences.zh: 然後罷鄉吏之供需，校版籍之欺敝，不數月省簿成，即以其簿及苗稅則例上之總領所，自此賦役均矣。

translations.literal: Then he abolished village clerks’ requisitions, checked registration fraud, and within a few months the provincial register was completed. He submitted this register along with seed-tax regulations to the general fiscal office, and from then on tax and corvée duties were equalized.
translations.idiomatic: He then ended the village clerks’ exactions, corrected fraud in the household registers, and within a few months completed the county ledger. He sent that ledger and the seed-tax schedule to the general fiscal office, and from then on levies and corvée were fairly apportioned.

sentences.zh: 夙興，冠裳聽訟，發擿如神，故事無不依期結正，雖負者亦無不心服。

translations.literal: Rising early, he put on official robes to hear lawsuits; his uncovering of facts was like divine insight. Old cases were all settled on schedule, and even those who lost were inwardly convinced.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early, dressed in official robes, and heard lawsuits; his ability to expose hidden facts seemed almost uncanny. Backlogged cases were all closed on time, and even the losing parties accepted the verdicts in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 真德秀扁其堂曰“對越”。

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu inscribed his hall with the words “Facing the Supreme.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu wrote the plaque for his hall: “Facing the Supreme.”

sentences.zh: 將代，整治如始至。

translations.literal: When about to be replaced, he maintained order as at his first arrival.
translations.idiomatic: As his term drew to a close, he kept the county in order just as he had on first taking office.

sentences.zh: 歲杪，與百姓休息，閣債負，蠲租稅，釋囚係，恤生瘞死，崇孝勸睦，仁民厚俗之事，悉舉以行，形之榜揭，見者嗟歎。

translations.literal: At year’s end he granted the people rest: suspended debts, remitted rents and taxes, released prisoners, cared for the living and buried the dead, honored filial piety and encouraged neighborliness — all benevolent acts to enrich custom were fully carried out and posted on placards; those who saw them sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At year’s end he gave the people a respite: debts were set aside, rents and taxes remitted, prisoners released, the living cared for and the dead buried, filial piety honored and neighborly harmony encouraged. Every measure to benefit the people and improve local custom was carried out and posted on public notices, and all who read them sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 調提轄文思院，幹辦諸軍審計，添差通判撫州，以言者罷，與祠。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise the Wensi Office, handling army audits; additionally assigned as vice-prefect of Fuzhou; removed due to critics; granted a temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to oversee the Wensi Office and handle audits for the various armies, he was also given an additional assignment as vice-prefect of Fuzhou. Critics brought about his removal, and he was granted a sinecure at a temple.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，通判蘄州。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, after the mourning period ended, he became vice-prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother and completing the mourning period, he served as vice-prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 時江右峒寇為亂，吉州八邑，七被殘毀，差知吉州，應鈴慨然曰：“此豈臣子辭難時耶？

translations.literal: At that time the stockade bandits of Jiangyou were in rebellion; of Jizhou’s eight counties, seven were ravaged. Appointed magistrate of Jizhou, Yingling said with feeling: “Is this a time for subjects to decline difficult posts?
translations.idiomatic: At the time the stockade bandits of Jiangyou were in revolt. Seven of Jizhou’s eight counties had been devastated. When appointed prefect of Jizhou, Yingling said with feeling, “Is this a moment when a subject should shrink from a hard assignment?

sentences.zh: ”即奉親以行。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he took his parents and set out.
translations.idiomatic: ” He at once set out, taking his parents with him.

sentences.zh: 下車，首以練兵、足食為先務，然後去冗吏，核軍籍，汰老弱，以次罷行。

translations.literal: Upon taking office, he first made drilling troops and securing provisions his priority, then removed redundant clerks, verified military registers, eliminated the old and weak, and dismissed them in order.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he first made training troops and securing provisions his top priorities, then cut redundant clerks, checked the military rolls, weeded out the aged and infirm, and dismissed them in due order.

sentences.zh: 應鈴洞究財計本末，每鄙榷酤興利，蘄五邑悉改為戶。

translations.literal: Yingling thoroughly investigated the roots of fiscal affairs and always despised profiting from liquor monopolies; all five counties of Qizhou were changed to household-based taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Yingling traced fiscal matters to their source and always scorned profiting from liquor monopolies. All five counties under Qizhou were converted from monopoly levies to household-based taxation.

sentences.zh: 吉，舟車之會，且屯大軍，六萬戶，人勸之榷，應鈴曰：“理財正辭，吾縱不能禁百姓群飲，其可誘之利其贏耶？

translations.literal: Jizhou was a hub of boats and carts and also stationed a large army — sixty thousand households. People urged him to establish a monopoly. Yingling said: “In managing finances one must speak correctly — even if I cannot forbid the people from drinking together, how could I use profit to lure them and skim off their earnings?
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou was a junction of river and road traffic and also quartered a large army — sixty thousand households. People urged him to institute a liquor monopoly. Yingling said, “In managing revenue one must speak honestly. Even if I cannot stop the people from drinking together, how could I tempt them with profit and feed on their gains?

sentences.zh: ”永新禾山群盜嘯聚，數日間應者以千數。

translations.literal: ” Bandits of Heshan in Yongxin gathered in droves; within days those who responded numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: ” In Yongxin, bandits of Heshan rallied in force; within days their followers numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 應鈴察過客趙希邵有才略，檄之攝邑，調郡兵，結隅保，分道搗其巢穴，禽之，誅其為首者七人，一鄉以定。

translations.literal: Yingling observed that the traveler Zhao Xishao had talent and strategy; he dispatched him to act as county magistrate, mobilized prefectural troops, organized corner guards, sent forces by separate routes to strike their lairs, captured them, executed seven ringleaders, and the township was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yingling saw that the traveler Zhao Xishao had ability and resourcefulness. He commissioned him to act as county magistrate, called up prefectural troops, organized local defense units, and sent columns by different routes to smash their hideouts. The ringleaders were captured; seven chief offenders were executed, and the township was pacified.

sentences.zh: 贛叛卒朱先賊殺主帥，應鈴曰：“此非小變也。

translations.literal: A mutinous soldier of Gan, Zhu Xian, murdered the commanding general as a bandit. Yingling said: “This is no minor incident.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xian, a mutinous soldier from Gan, killed his commander and turned bandit. Yingling said, “This is no small disturbance.

sentences.zh: ”密遣諜以厚賞捕之。

translations.literal: ” He secretly sent spies with generous rewards to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He secretly sent agents with rich rewards to seize him.

sentences.zh: 部使者劾其輕發，鐫一官。

translations.literal: The circuit envoy impeached him for acting rashly; his rank was reduced by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit commissioner impeached him for acting precipitously, and his rank was reduced by one step.

sentences.zh: 閑居六年，養親讀書，泊如也。

translations.literal: He lived in retirement for six years, caring for his parents and reading books, calm and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for six years, supporting his parents and reading at leisure, serene and unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 起廣西提點刑獄，力辭，逾年乃拜命。

translations.literal: Appointed Guangxi judicial intendant; he strenuously declined; only after more than a year did he accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Guangxi judicial intendant, he declined firmly; only after more than a year did he accept the commission.

sentences.zh: 既至，多所平反，丁錢蠹民，力奏免之。

translations.literal: Once there, he reversed many wrongful convictions; the ding money was a scourge on the people — he memorialized strenuously to have it abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After arriving, he reversed many unjust verdicts. The ding money oppressed the people, and he memorialized forcefully to have it abolished.

sentences.zh: 召為金部郎官，入見，首言：“今以朝行暮改之規模，欲變累年上玩下慢之積習；

translations.literal: Summoned as Jinbu lang official; upon audience, he first said: “Today, with a pattern of changing policy morning and evening, one seeks to transform accumulated customs of superiors being lax and subordinates being insolent over many years;
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to serve as a Jinbu lang official, on entering audience he first said, “Today, with policies that change from morning to evening, you wish to overturn customs built up over years in which superiors were indulgent and subordinates contemptuous;

sentences.zh: 以悠悠內治之敝政，欲圖一旦赫赫外攘之大功。

translations.literal: with languid defective internal governance, one seeks to plan in a single day magnificent external achievements against foreign foes.
translations.idiomatic: with slack and failing domestic administration, you wish to plan in a single day a glorious campaign of external conquest.

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“公論不出於君子，而參以逢君之小人；

translations.literal: ” He also said: “Public opinion does not come from gentlemen, but is mixed with sycophantic petty men;
translations.idiomatic: ” He also said, “Public opinion no longer comes from upright men, but is mixed with flatterers who please the ruler;

sentences.zh: 紀綱不正於朝廷，而牽於弄權之閹寺。

translations.literal: discipline is not set right at court, but is constrained by power-grasping eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: and discipline is not restored at court, but is held hostage by eunuchs who manipulate power.

sentences.zh: ”言皆讜直，識者韙之。

translations.literal: ” His words were all candid and upright; perceptive men approved of them.
translations.idiomatic: ” His words were blunt and forthright, and thoughtful men applauded them.

sentences.zh: 遷尚左郎官，尋為浙東提點刑獄，力丐便養，改直秘閣、江西提舉常平，並詭挾三萬戶，風采凜然。

translations.literal: Promoted to Shangzuo lang official; soon appointed Zhedong judicial intendant; he strenuously begged for convenient care of parents; reassigned as Direct Secretarial Associate and Jiangxi grain intendant, concurrently holding an irregular triplicate assignment over thirty thousand households; his bearing was awe-inspiring.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Shangzuo lang official, he was soon appointed Zhedong judicial intendant but begged hard for a post that would let him care for his parents. He was reassigned as Direct Secretarial Associate and Jiangxi grain intendant, holding at once an unusual cluster of duties over thirty thousand households, and his bearing was formidable.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服除，遷軍器監兼尚左郎官，召見，奏曰：“國事大且急者，儲貳為先。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his father, after the mourning period ended, he was transferred to director of the Armaments Directorate while concurrently holding Shangzuo lang official; summoned to audience, he memorialized: “Among state affairs that are great and urgent, establishing the heir apparent comes first.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father and completing the mourning period, he was transferred to director of the Armaments Directorate while retaining his post as Shangzuo lang official. Summoned to audience, he memorialized, “Of the great and urgent affairs of state, establishing the heir apparent comes first.

sentences.zh: 陛下不斷自宸衷，徒眩惑於左右近習之言，轉移於宮庭嬪禦之見，失今不圖，奸臣乘夜半，片紙或從中出，忠義之士束手無策矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not decide from the depths of your heart but is merely dazzled and confused by the words of close attendants at your side, swayed by the views of palace consorts, and fails to plan now, treacherous ministers may at midnight produce a slip of paper from within the palace, and loyal men will be left helpless.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not decide from your own inner conviction but is dazzled by the talk of close attendants, swayed by the opinions of palace women, and lets the moment pass, treacherous ministers may at midnight produce an order from within the palace, and loyal men will have no recourse.

sentences.zh: ”帝為之動容。

translations.literal: ” The emperor was moved in expression.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor’s expression changed at his words.

sentences.zh: 屬鹽法屢變，商賈之贏，上奪於朝廷之自鬻，下奪於都郡之拘留；

translations.literal: As the salt laws changed repeatedly, merchants’ profits were seized above by the court’s direct sale and below by the detention of goods in capital prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Because the salt laws changed again and again, merchants’ profits were taken from above by the court’s direct sale of salt and from below by the detention of goods in metropolitan prefectures;

sentences.zh: 九江、豫章扼其襟喉，江右貧民終歲食淡，商與民俱困矣。

translations.literal: Jiujiang and Yuzhang controlled the strategic passages; the poor people of Jiangyou ate plain food all year, and both merchants and commoners were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang and Yuzhang straddled the vital routes, and the poor of Jiangyou ate sparingly all year long. Merchants and commoners alike were worn down.

sentences.zh: 應鈴力陳四害，願用祖宗入粟易鹽之法。

translations.literal: Yingling strenuously set forth four harms and wished to use the ancestral method of exchanging grain for salt.
translations.idiomatic: Yingling forcefully enumerated four evils and urged a return to the ancestral system of exchanging grain for salt.

sentences.zh: 授直寶謨閣，湖南轉運判官兼安撫司。

translations.literal: He was granted Direct Baomo Pavilion and appointed transport vice-commissioner of Hunan while also serving on the pacification staff.
translations.idiomatic: Granted the title Direct Baomo Pavilion, he was made Hunan transport vice-commissioner with concurrent duties on the pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 峒獠蔣、何三族聚千餘人，執縣令，殺王官，帥憲招捕，逾年不至，應鈴曰：“ 招之適以長寇，亟捕之可也。

translations.literal: The stockade tribes Jiang and He, three clans gathering more than a thousand men, seized the county magistrate and killed a court official. The intendant and judicial commissioner tried summons and capture for more than a year without success. Yingling said: “Summoning them will only embolden the bandits; they should be captured at once.
translations.idiomatic: Three clans of stockade people, the Jiang and He families, gathered more than a thousand men, seized the county magistrate, and killed a court official. The intendant and judicial commissioner tried negotiation and capture for over a year without result. Yingling said, “Summoning them will only encourage the rebels. They must be seized quickly.

sentences.zh: ”即調飛虎等軍會隅總討之，應鈴親臨誓師，號令明壯，士卒鼓勇以前，禽蔣時選父子及凶渠五人誅之，脅從者使之安業，未一月全師而歸。

translations.literal: ” He at once mobilized the Flying Tiger and other armies to join the local defense forces in a general punitive campaign. Yingling personally came to rally the troops; his orders were clear and forceful, the soldiers advanced with high morale, Jiang Shixuan father and son and five chief ringleaders were captured and executed, the coerced followers were allowed to resume their livelihoods, and within less than a month the whole force returned intact.
translations.idiomatic: ” He immediately mobilized the Flying Tiger Army and others to join local defense units in a joint campaign. Yingling personally came to exhort the troops; his commands were clear and bold, and the soldiers pressed forward with spirit. Jiang Shixuan, his son, and five chief ringleaders were captured and executed; those who had been coerced were allowed to return to their occupations, and in less than a month the entire force returned without loss.

sentences.zh: 授直煥章閣，上疏謝事，不允；

translations.literal: Granted Direct Huanzhang Pavilion, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; it was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Granted Direct Huanzhang Pavilion, he submitted a memorial asking to retire; the request was denied;

sentences.zh: 擢大理少卿，再請又不允。

translations.literal: promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review; he requested again and again was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review; he asked again, and again was refused.

sentences.zh: 一旦籍府庫，核簿書，處決官事已，遂及家務，纖悉不遺。

translations.literal: One day he inventoried the treasury, checked the ledgers, settled official business, then turned to household affairs, leaving nothing large or small unattended.
translations.idiomatic: One day he took stock of the treasury, checked the account books, finished all official business, then turned to his household affairs, leaving nothing undone, however small.

sentences.zh: 僚屬勸以清心省事，曰：“生死，數也，平生學力，正在今日。

translations.literal: Subordinates urged him to clear his mind and reduce his burdens. He said: “Life and death are a matter of fate; the learning of a lifetime is tested precisely today.
translations.idiomatic: His staff urged him to ease his mind and leave business aside. He said, “Life and death are fate’s decree; a lifetime of learning is proved precisely today.

sentences.zh: ”帥別之傑問疾，應鈴整冠肅入，言論如平常，之傑退，倏然而逝。

translations.literal: ” The intendant Bie Zhijie came to inquire after his illness. Yingling straightened his cap and entered with solemnity; his speech was as usual. When Zhijie withdrew, he suddenly passed away.
translations.idiomatic: ” Intendant Bie Zhijie came to visit him in illness. Yingling straightened his cap and received him with composure, speaking as he always had. After Zhijie left, he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 應鈴開明磊落，守正不阿，別白是非，見義必為，不以得失利害動其心。

translations.literal: Yingling was open, bright, and upright, holding to the correct path without bending; he distinguished right from wrong, and when he saw righteousness he acted — gain, loss, benefit, and harm did not move his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yingling was open and upright, steadfast and unyielding. He distinguished right from wrong, acted whenever justice required it, and was unmoved by gain, loss, or personal interest.

sentences.zh: 書饋不交上官，薦舉不徇權門，當官而行，無敢撓以非義。

translations.literal: He did not exchange letters and gifts with superiors, nor did he currying favor with powerful families in recommendations; he acted according to office, and none dared obstruct him with improper means.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged no letters or gifts with superiors and did not recommend people to please powerful families. He did his duty as an official, and no one dared interfere with improper pressure.

sentences.zh: 所至無留訟，無滯獄，繩吏不少貸，亦未嚐沒其貲，曰：“彼之貨以悖入，官又從而悖入之，可乎？

translations.literal: Wherever he served there were no lingering lawsuits and no backlog in the prisons. He did not lightly pardon corrupt officials, yet he never confiscated their property, saying: “Their goods were gained by wrongdoing — should the state then take them by wrongdoing as well?
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, lawsuits did not linger and prisons did not backlog. He showed no leniency to corrupt clerks, yet he never seized their property, saying, “Their wealth was gained unjustly — should the government then take it unjustly too?

sentences.zh: ”進修潔，案奸贓，振樹風聲，聞者興起。

translations.literal: ” He promoted integrity, investigated graft, and raised the standard of public conduct; those who heard of it were inspired.
translations.idiomatic: ” He upheld integrity, investigated corruption, and set a moral example that stirred those who heard of it.

sentences.zh: 家居時，人有不平，不走官府，而走應鈴之門；

translations.literal: When at home, people with grievances did not go to the government but came to Yingling’s door;
translations.idiomatic: While living at home, people with grievances did not go to the magistrates but came to Yingling’s door;

sentences.zh: 為不善者，輒相戒曰：“無使範公聞之。

translations.literal: those who meant to do wrong would warn one another: “Do not let Master Fan hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: and wrongdoers would warn one another, “Don’t let Master Fan find out.

sentences.zh: ”讀書明大義，尤喜《左氏春秋》，所著有《西堂雜著》十卷，斷訟語曰《對越集》四十九卷。

translations.literal: ” He read books and understood great principles, especially loving the 《Zuo Tradition》, and his writings included ten juan of 《Miscellaneous Writings from the Western Hall》 and forty-nine juan of judicial remarks titled 《Facing the Supreme Collection》.
translations.idiomatic: ” He read widely and grasped the larger moral principles, especially favoring the 《Zuo Tradition》. His works included ten juan of 《Miscellaneous Writings from the Western Hall》 and forty-nine juan of judicial remarks titled 《Facing the Supreme Collection》.

sentences.zh: 徐鹿卿曰：“應鈴經術似兒寬，決獄似雋不疑，治民似龔遂，風采似范滂，理財似劉晏，而正大過之。

translations.literal: Xu Luqing said: “Yingling’s mastery of the classics resembled Er Kuan, his adjudication of cases resembled Juan Buyi, his governance of the people resembled Gong Sui, his bearing resembled Fan Pang, his management of finances resembled Liu Yan — yet he surpassed them all in rectitude and greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Luqing said, “In classical learning Yingling was like Er Kuan; in judging cases like Juan Buyi; in governing the people like Gong Sui; in moral bearing like Fan Pang; in managing revenue like Liu Yan — yet in uprightness and breadth he surpassed them all.

sentences.zh: ”人以為名言。

translations.literal: ” People regarded it as a celebrated remark.
translations.idiomatic: ” People took this for a memorable saying.

sentences.zh: 徐經孫，字中立，初名子柔。

translations.literal: Xu Jingsun, style name Zhongli, originally named Zirou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingsun, whose style name was Zhongli, was originally named Zirou.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年進士，授瀏陽主簿，潭守俾部牙契錢至州，有告者曰：“朝廷方下令頒行十七界會，令若此錢皆用會，小須，則幸而獲大利矣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Baoqing, he was appointed chief clerk of Liuyang. The Tan prefect ordered him to convey tooth-contract money to the prefecture. An informer said: “The court has just ordered the issue of the seventeenth series of paper notes. If all this money is exchanged for notes, a little delay will fortunately yield great profit.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the second year of Baoqing (1226), he was appointed chief clerk of Liuyang. The prefect of Tanzhou ordered him to convey tooth-contract money to the prefectural seat. Someone told him, “The court has just ordered the circulation of the seventeenth issue of paper notes. If you exchange all this money for notes and wait a little, you may reap a large profit.

sentences.zh: ”經孫曰：“此錢取諸保司，出諸公庫，吾納會而私取其錢，外欺其民，內欺其心，奚可哉！

translations.literal: ” Jingsun said: “This money was taken from the security office and issued from the public treasury. If I turn in notes and privately keep the cash, I would deceive the people outwardly and my own heart inwardly — how could I do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: ” Jingsun said, “This money was taken from the security office and drawn from the public treasury. If I submit notes and keep the cash for myself, I would cheat the people without and betray my own conscience within. How could I do that!

sentences.zh: ”詰旦，悉以所部錢上之，其人驚服有愧色。

translations.literal: ” At dawn the next day he turned over all the money under his charge; the man was astonished, convinced, and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The next morning he remitted all the money under his charge. The informer was astonished, convinced, and ashamed.

sentences.zh: 辟永興令，知臨武縣，通判潭州。

translations.literal: Recruited as magistrate of Yongxing, he served as magistrate of Linwu County and vice-prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited to serve as magistrate of Yongxing, he later became magistrate of Linwu County and vice-prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 帥陳韡雅相知，事必谘而後行。

translations.literal: Intendant Chen Wei held him in high regard and consulted him on every matter before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Intendant Chen Wei respected him deeply and consulted him before taking action on any matter.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，由豐儲倉提管進權轄，國子博士兼資善堂直講。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he advanced from manager of the Fengchu Granary to acting supervisor, then to erudite of the Directorate of Education while concurrently lecturer at the Zishan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he rose from manager of the Fengchu Granary to acting supervisor, then became erudite of the Directorate of Education while also serving as lecturer at the Zishan Hall.

sentences.zh: 為監察御史，劾京尹厲文翁言偽而辨，疏入，留中。

translations.literal: As investigating censor, he impeached the capital intendant Li Wenweng for eloquent but false speech; the memorial entered but was held at court.
translations.idiomatic: As investigating censor, he impeached the capital intendant Li Wenweng for clever but deceptive speech. The memorial was submitted but kept at court.

sentences.zh: 宣諭至再，即日出關，上遣使追之，不及。

translations.literal: Imperial instructions came twice; that very day he left the pass. The emperor sent messengers to pursue him but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial messages came twice, but that same day he crossed the border out of office. The emperor sent messengers to recall him, but they could not catch up.

sentences.zh: 進直寶章閣、福建提點刑獄，號稱平允。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Baozhang Pavilion and Fujian judicial intendant, he was praised as fair and even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Direct Baozhang Pavilion and Fujian judicial intendant, he won a reputation for fairness.

sentences.zh: 歲餘升安撫使，召為秘書監兼太子諭德。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to pacification commissioner and summoned as director of the Secretariat while concurrently tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he was promoted to pacification commissioner and summoned to serve as director of the Secretariat while also tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 經孫為安撫時，韡家居，門人故吏有撓法者不得逞，相與搖撼。

translations.literal: When Jingsun served as pacification commissioner, Wei was living at home. Former students and subordinates who had evaded the law could not have their way and together worked to undermine him.
translations.idiomatic: While Jingsun was pacification commissioner, Wei was retired at home. Former protégés and subordinates who had bent the law found themselves blocked and joined in efforts to shake him.

sentences.zh: 至是韡起家判本郡，懷私逞忿，無復交承之禮，即日劾奏通判，語侵經孫，謂席卷府庫而去，於是罷通判，削其秩。

translations.literal: At this point Wei rose from retirement to serve as judge of his home prefecture, harboring private resentment and venting anger, no longer observing the rites of transfer of office. That very day he memorialized impeaching the vice-prefect; his language impugned Jingsun, alleging that he had swept the treasury clean on departure. Thereupon the vice-prefect was dismissed and his rank reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wei left retirement to serve as judge of his home prefecture, nursing private grievances and venting his anger, no longer observing the proper rites of transfer. That same day he memorialized against the vice-prefect, his language touching Jingsun and accusing him of emptying the treasury on departure. The vice-prefect was dismissed and demoted.

sentences.zh: 經孫造朝，具白於政府。

translations.literal: Jingsun went to court and fully reported the matter to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsun went to court and laid the whole matter before the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 事上聞，帝大怒，諭宰執曰：“陳韡老繆至此，宜亟罷之。

translations.literal: When the affair reached the emperor, he was greatly angered and instructed the chief councilors: “Chen Wei has become so muddled in old age that he should be removed at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the emperor, he was furious and told the chief councilors, “Chen Wei has grown so senile and confused that he should be dismissed immediately.

sentences.zh: ”於是經孫再詣政府，言：“某，韡門生也，前日之白，公事也，苟韡以是得罪，人謂我何？

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Jingsun went again to the chief ministers and said: “I am Wei’s student. My report the other day was a public matter. If Wei should be punished for it, what will people say of me?
translations.idiomatic: ” Jingsun then went again to the chief ministers and said, “I am Wei’s student. My report the other day concerned public business. If Wei is punished because of it, what will people think of me?

sentences.zh: ”請之不置，俾自乞閑，明通判無罪，識者韙之。

translations.literal: ” He pleaded repeatedly without cease, had Wei request retirement on his own, and made clear the vice-prefect’s innocence; perceptive men approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He pleaded without stopping, had Wei ask on his own for a retirement post, and made clear that the vice-prefect was innocent. Thoughtful men applauded him.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正少卿、起居舍人、起居郎，入奏：“君人者當守理欲之界限。

translations.literal: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, diarist, and court gentleman for attendance, he entered memorial: “One who rules others should keep to the boundary between principle and desire.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, diarist, and attendance gentleman, he memorialized on entering office, “A ruler should observe the boundary between principle and desire.

sentences.zh: ”遷刑部侍郎兼給事中，升太子左庶子、太子詹事，輔導東宮者三年，敷陳經義，隨事啟迪。

translations.literal: ” Promoted to vice minister of punishments while concurrently receiving edicts, then elevated to left tutor and grand tutor of the crown prince; for three years he instructed the Eastern Palace, expounding the classics and offering guidance as occasions arose.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was promoted to vice minister of punishments while concurrently receiving edicts, then to left tutor and grand tutor of the crown prince. For three years he guided the Eastern Palace, expounding the classics and offering counsel as occasions arose.

sentences.zh: 太子入侍，必以其所講聞悉奏之，帝未嚐不稱善。

translations.literal: Whenever the crown prince attended the emperor, he always reported in full what had been discussed; the emperor never failed to express approval.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the crown prince attended the emperor, Jingsun always reported everything they had discussed, and the emperor invariably expressed approval.

sentences.zh: 景定三年春雷，詔求直言，經孫對曰：“三數年來，言論者以靖共為主，有懷者以嘩訐為戒，忠讜之氣，鬱不得行，上帝降監，假雷以鳴。

translations.literal: In spring thunder struck in the third year of Jingding, and an edict sought forthright speech. Jingsun replied: “For several years now, those who spoke in court have made quiet compliance their aim, and those with honest views have taken noisy accusation as a warning. The spirit of loyal candor has been stifled and cannot prevail. Heaven has sent down its watch, using thunder to sound the alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When spring thunder sounded in the third year of Jingding (1262), an edict called for frank counsel. Jingsun replied, “For several years speakers in court have made quiet compliance their standard, while those with honest views have been warned against clamorous accusation. The spirit of loyal remonstrance has been suppressed and cannot act. Heaven has sent down its warning, using thunder to sound the alarm.

sentences.zh: ”切中時病。

translations.literal: ” His words struck directly at the ailments of the time.
translations.idiomatic: ” His words cut straight to the sickness of the age.

sentences.zh: 公田法行，經孫條其利害，忤丞相賈似道，拜翰林學士、知制誥，未逾月，諷御史舒有開奏免，罷歸。

translations.literal: When the public-fields law was implemented, Jingsun itemized its harms and benefits, offending Chief Councilor Jia Sidao. He was appointed Hanlin academician and drafter of edicts; within a month the censor Shu Youkai was prompted to memorialize for his removal, and he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When the public-fields policy was put into effect, Jingsun listed its advantages and harms, offending Chief Councilor Jia Sidao. He was appointed Hanlin academician and drafter of edicts, but within a month the censor Shu Youkai was prompted to memorialize for his removal, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 授湖南安撫使、知潭州，不拜。

translations.literal: Appointed Hunan pacification commissioner and magistrate of Tanzhou, he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Hunan pacification commissioner and magistrate of Tanzhou, he declined the commission.

sentences.zh: 授端明殿大學士，閑居十年，卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Granted the title academician of the Duanming Hall, he lived in retirement for ten years, died, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Granted the title academician of the Duanming Hall, he lived in retirement for ten years, then died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 經孫所薦陳茂濂為公田官，分司嘉興，聞經孫去國，曰：我不可以負徐公。

translations.literal: Chen Maolian, whom Jingsun had recommended as public-fields official and assigned to Jiaxing, upon hearing that Jingsun had left office said: I cannot fail Master Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Maolian, whom Jingsun had recommended as public-fields official and posted to Jiaxing, on hearing that Jingsun had left office said, “I cannot betray Master Xu.

sentences.zh: ”遂以親老謝歸，終身不起。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he pleaded old parents and returned home, never taking office again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then pleaded aged parents and resigned, never holding office again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 論曰：嗚呼，寧宗之為君，韓侂胄之為相，豈用兵之時乎？

translations.literal: The commentary says: Alas — was Ningzong as ruler, or Han Tuozhou as chief councilor, truly a time for launching war?
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Alas — with Ningzong as ruler and Han Tuozhou as chief councilor, was this truly a time to go to war?

sentences.zh: 故婁機力止之。

translations.literal: Therefore Lou Ji strove to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Lou Ji worked hard to stop it.

sentences.zh: 小學之廢久矣，而機獨知致力於此。

translations.literal: The Elementary Learning had long been neglected, yet Ji alone knew to devote himself to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Elementary Learning had long fallen into neglect, yet Ji alone devoted himself to reviving it.

sentences.zh: 沈煥、舒璘學遠識明。

translations.literal: Shen Huan and Shu Lin had learning far-reaching and insight clear.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huan and Shu Lin possessed far-reaching learning and clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 曹彥約可與建立事功。

translations.literal: Cao Yanyue was capable of establishing achievements in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yanyue was a man capable of accomplishing practical results.

sentences.zh: 範應鈴赫然政事如神明。

translations.literal: Fan Yingling’s administrative achievements were brilliant as if divine.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yingling’s governance was brilliant, as though guided by a spirit.

sentences.zh: 徐經孫清慎有守，卒以爭公田迕賈似道去國，君子稱之。

translations.literal: Xu Jingsun was pure, cautious, and principled; he ultimately left office by opposing the public-fields policy and offending Jia Sidao, and men of worth praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingsun was pure, cautious, and steadfast; he ultimately left office after opposing the public-fields policy and running afoul of Jia Sidao, and worthy men praised him for it.
